verdict: Domino's grew revenue 3.4% to $1,186M on its supply chain and 175 net new stores, and buybacks helped earnings per share rise 13% to $4.60 even though same-store sales barely grew.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $1,186M, vs $1,147M a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $4.08 a year ago — helped by a 3% lower share count from buybacks

kpis.label: Global retail sales
kpis.note: What all stores sold, up 3.2% excluding currency effects — most of it belongs to franchisees, not Domino's itself

kpis.label: Net new stores
kpis.note: 26 net in the U.S. and 149 international in the quarter — 22,706 stores worldwide

segments.name: Supply chain
segments.note: Selling dough, cheese and toppings to franchise stores — the biggest revenue line. Up 7% on higher order volumes and a 2.2% rise in food-basket prices charged to stores.

segments.name: U.S. franchise royalties & fees
segments.note: Royalties and fees from U.S. franchised stores — nearly pure profit, since franchisees bear the store costs. Up 5% on store growth.

segments.name: U.S. franchise advertising
segments.note: Contributions from U.S. franchisees into the national advertising fund. Every dollar is spent on advertising, so it shows up again as a matching cost below.

segments.name: International franchise royalties & fees
segments.note: Royalties from franchised stores outside the U.S. Up 7% as 149 net new international stores opened in the quarter.

segments.name: U.S. Company-owned stores
segments.note: Sales at the 187 stores Domino's runs itself. Down 26% because some company-owned markets were sold to franchisees (refranchised) in Q2 2026.

opex.name: U.S. franchise advertising
opex.note: Spending the advertising fund collected from franchisees — it mirrors the advertising revenue line above almost dollar for dollar.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — headquarters, technology and support for stores. Flat vs $105M a year ago.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $44M on Domino's borrowings, plus $3M of other expense (including a small refranchising loss) — a net $47M cost.
follow100Note: The rows add to $99.99 due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The supply chain is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Supply-chain revenue rose 7% to $746M — 63% of all revenue — on more orders and higher food-basket prices, and its gross margin widened 0.9 points to 12.2% on procurement savings. Royalty income, the high-margin core, grew 5% in the U.S. and 7% internationally.

takeaways.title: Same-store sales barely grew
takeaways.text: U.S. same-store sales rose just 0.3% (company stores +1.0%, franchised +0.3%) and international 0.2% excluding currency. Growth came from new stores — 175 net openings took the system to 22,706 stores — not from existing stores selling much more.

takeaways.title: Buybacks flatter the per-share line
takeaways.text: Net income rose 9% to $152M, but EPS rose 13% to $4.60 because buybacks cut the diluted share count 3% to 33.1M. Operating income grew 8% to $242M despite the drag from selling company-owned stores to franchisees.

oneTimers: Domino's refranchised certain U.S. company-owned store markets in Q2 2026, booking a small $0.2M refranchising loss in Q3. That portfolio change — not weaker demand — is why company-owned store revenue fell 26% YoY.
footerNote: Figures are rounded to $M; cost of revenue absorbs a $1M rounding increase and franchise advertising expense a $1M rounding decrease so the lines add exactly. The quarter is Domino's fiscal Q3, ended September 6, 2026.
